svg.title: Can a from-scratch engine replace Python's re, and is it faster?
svg.desc: Python 3.14.6 passes its complete 31,237-check reference. The current Rust, C, and corrected Zig engines were each independently built identically twice; this is build evidence, not a passed compatibility test. Rust has 7,461 verified passing checks, 2,042 actual matching differences, and five failed groups. C has 7,197 verified passes, 2,094 matching differences, and six failed groups. Zig has 3,583 verified passes, 1,764 actual matching differences, and seven failed groups. Its parent controller rejected the nested publication field. The separately authenticated interpreter child really ran 385 calls but failed to restore the original matcher during cleanup; neither infrastructure failure adds an invented matching difference. All failed engines, previous C failures, and Zig build history remain preserved. C++, Go, and an independently authored Fortran tokenizer, compiler and matching engine exist as source only; none has been built, tested, or qualified. Fortran is outside the frozen independence audit and candidate gate. No replacement is qualified. Candidate speed, memory, confidence intervals, and the final holdout have not been measured or opened. The 1.5-times marker is a goal, never a result.
svg.text: Can these engines replace Python re?
Current source-built evidence against Python 3.14.6 | no outside regex engines
1. Does it work exactly like Python?
The same complete 31,237-check test applies to every engine. Grey means not tested, never zero passes.
Reference implementation; complete frozen test passed
